title: Loop over storage with a trip count the contract does not bound
rationale: A Soroban invocation has a fixed budget — instructions, memory and the number of ledger entries it may touch — and a loop whose count comes from an argument, a caller-supplied collection or a value in storage does not fit inside it until the transaction is already running. The failure happens after the caller pays, on a network where the caller cannot know the count in advance, and the input that causes it is one the contract accepts. On a blockchain this is worse than an ordinary performance bug: the trap is reachable by anyone, it costs the attacker nothing but fees, and the entrypoint that would let the contract be repaired is often the one that no longer completes. The check is structural — a loop whose bound is not a literal, with a storage call in the body — but deciding that a storage call is what the loop is for is a judgement, and iterating a collection built inside the function is a false positive it will make, so the rule is marked as a heuristic.
remediation: Bound the work: take a fixed-size batch per call (`for i in 0..BATCH`), keep an explicit cursor in storage so the caller can resume, and reject the input that would exceed the batch with a clear error. If the loop genuinely must iterate over a caller-supplied collection, cap the collection at the entrypoint.
